subject: History
description: Chandragupta I to Skandagupta, Samudragupta's conquests, Aryabhata, Kalidasa, Nalanda

questions.stem: The Gupta dynasty was founded around 320 CE by:

options.option_text: Chandragupta I (married Lichchhavi princess Kumaradevi, took title 'Maharajadhiraja')

questions.explanation: Chandragupta I (~320 CE) — true founder of imperial Guptas. Sri Gupta + Ghatotkacha were earlier (3rd C, ruled small territory). Marriage to Lichchhavi (Vaishali) princess KUMARADEVI brought legitimacy + territory. Issued gold 'King-Queen' coins. Took 'Maharajadhiraja' (great king of kings). Started Gupta era from 319-320 CE. Gupta age (320-550 CE) often called 'Classical / Golden Age' for arts, literature, science, mathematics, governance.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The 'Napoleon of India' — for his vast military conquests detailed in the Allahabad/Prayag Prashasti — was:
questions.explanation: Samudragupta — son of Chandragupta I. Title 'Napoleon of India' coined by V.A. Smith. Allahabad / Prayag Pillar Inscription (composed by his court poet Harisena, engraved on Ashoka's own pillar) details his conquests: 9 Aryavarta kings 'uprooted', 12 Dakshinapatha kings 'liberated and reinstated' (Dharma-vijaya), Aksharaja-Kachakuri's 5 chiefdoms, forest tribes, frontier states, foreign powers (Saka, Kushans). Performed Ashvamedha sacrifice. Issued 8 types of gold coins — Tiger, Lyre-player, Ashvamedha, etc. Title 'Kaviraja' — Sanskrit-loving poet-king.

questions.stem: Chandragupta II 'Vikramaditya' is best known for:

options.option_text: Defeating the Sakas, marrying Naga princess, supporting 'Navaratnas' incl. Kalidasa

questions.explanation: Chandragupta II (~380-415 CE) — son of Samudragupta. Defeated the Western Kshatrapas (Sakas) of Gujarat-Saurashtra (campaign celebrated by 'Vikramaditya' title). Issued silver coins after the Saka conquest — first Gupta silver. Married Kuberanaga (Naga); daughter Prabhavati married Vakataka king (matrimonial alliance). His court hosted 'Navaratnas' (Nine Gems): Kalidasa, Varahamihira, Amarasimha, Dhanvantari, Vetala Bhatta, Ghatakarpara, Kshapanaka, Shanku, Vararuchi. Chinese pilgrim Faxian (Fa-Hien) visited his empire (~399-414 CE).

questions.stem: The famous mathematician-astronomer who computed π ≈ 3.1416 and proposed Earth's rotation in his 'Aryabhatiya' (499 CE) was:
questions.explanation: Aryabhata I (b. 476 CE) — wrote Aryabhatiya (in 121 verses) at age 23. Key contributions: π ≈ 3.1416 ('asanna' = approximate); concept of zero as a placeholder; place-value decimal system fully formed; Earth rotates on its axis (heliocentric ideas anticipating Copernicus); approximate sin(x) tables; lengths of solar / sidereal year. Bhaskara I (~600 CE) wrote commentaries. Brahmagupta (628 CE) gave first explicit rules for arithmetic with zero + negative numbers. Bhaskara II (12th C) wrote Lilavati. Varahamihira (~505 CE) — astronomy + meteorology (Brihat Samhita, Pancha Siddhantika).

questions.stem: Kalidasa — Sanskrit's greatest dramatist — wrote which of the following plays?

options.option_text: Abhijnanasakuntalam (Recognition of Sakuntala) and Meghaduta (Cloud Messenger)

questions.explanation: Kalidasa's major works: Plays — Abhijnanasakuntalam (most celebrated), Vikramorvashiyam, Malavikagnimitram. Epic poems — Raghuvamsha, Kumarasambhava. Lyric — Meghaduta (Cloud Messenger), Ritusamhara. Translated to English by William Jones (1789) — Sakuntala caused a sensation in Europe; Goethe famously praised it. Mricchakatika ('The Little Clay Cart') — by Sudraka. Mudrarakshasa (about Chanakya overthrow of Nandas) — by Vishakhadatta. Gita Govinda — by Jayadeva (12th C, Krishna theme). Kalidasa is identified by tradition with court of Vikramaditya.

questions.stem: Nalanda University — one of the world's first major residential universities — was at its peak under the Guptas. Located in modern:
questions.explanation: Nalanda — Bihar, ~95 km SE of Patna. Founded under Kumaragupta I (5th C). Peak in 7th C — 10,000 students + 1,500 teachers. Specialised in Buddhist studies, medicine, astronomy, mathematics, philosophy, logic. Visited by Chinese pilgrims Xuanzang (Hiuen-Tsang, 7th C) and Yijing (I-Tsing). Library was 9-storeys tall — Dharmaganja. Sacked + burnt by Bakhtiyar Khilji (~1193 CE) — fire said to have lasted months. UNESCO WHS 2016. Modern Nalanda University revived 2014 (international university near old site). Other ancient universities — Takshashila (Taxila, Pakistan), Vikramshila, Odantapuri.

questions.stem: The Gupta Empire's decline began with the invasions of:

options.option_text: Hunas (White Huns) under Toramana and Mihirakula in late 5th-6th C

questions.explanation: Skandagupta (455-467 CE) — last great Gupta. Junagadh inscription mentions repair of Sudarshana lake (built by Chandragupta Maurya). Defeated the Hunas during his reign. After Skandagupta, successive Hun invasions weakened the empire — Toramana (early 6th C) and his son Mihirakula (~510-540 CE). Yashodharman of Malwa is credited with defeating Mihirakula (~528 CE). Combined with succession disputes + economic decline + rise of regional kingdoms (Vakatakas, Maukharis, later Harsha), Gupta empire dissolved by ~550 CE. Brief revival under Harshavardhana (606-647 CE) of Pushyabhuti dynasty.
